title: Deno before 2.7.14 on a Mac: a --deny-read, --deny-write, --deny-run or --deny-ffi rule misses the same file spelled another way (CVE-2026-49401)
summary: Deno's advisory GHSA-8xpq-cjcf-3wh9 (CVE-2026-49401, high, CWE-41 and CWE-176) says that before 2.7.14 its permission checks compared the path a program asked for with the path given to --deny-read, --deny-write, --deny-run or --deny-ffi byte for byte, while a Mac's disk (APFS) opens the same file for other spellings of its name: another Unicode form (an accented letter written as a letter and a combining accent), another case, a ligature (U+FB01 for fi) or ß for ss. A program Deno was told to keep out of a file could read or write it under another spelling. Deno 2.7.14 compares both paths in NFC with Unicode case folding; the advisory says Linux and Windows are not affected by this variant. CERT/CC lists it in VU#604762 (16 Nov 2026). CISA's catalog (2026.11.13) does not list it. A Deno below 2.7.14 on a Mac is EXPOSED; on Linux it is SAFE for this flaw, with that reason, since the advisory says Linux is not affected. A Deno whose version can't be read is UNKNOWN anywhere. Wardlatch reads Homebrew's Deno from the keg its opt link and its bin/deno link name, and a mise or asdf install (installs/deno/<version>/bin/deno) and the official installer's ~/.deno/bin/deno from the version Deno compiles into its own file, never from a folder's name, which need not match the program in it (the user agent Deno/<version>+<commit>, a constant in cli/lib/version.rs; read from Deno's source, not yet measured on a release build, so a build without it reads UNKNOWN, never SAFE); it never runs deno.

versionFiles.notAffectedOn: Deno's advisory says this flaw is on macOS only: Linux and Windows are not affected by it
versionFiles.fix: Update Deno to 2.7.14 or later: deno upgrade, or brew upgrade deno. Until then, on a Mac, use --allow-read, --allow-write, --allow-run and --allow-ffi lists instead of --deny-* rules (the advisory's own workaround).
versionFiles.lookedIn: Homebrew's opt/deno and bin/deno links, mise's and asdf's Deno installs, and ~/.deno/bin/deno

safeText: no Deno below 2.7.14 found in the places this check reads
notCovered: Deno installed another way (MacPorts, Nix, a binary copied somewhere else, the npm package), Deno compiled into a program with deno compile, and Deno inside other tools. Whether a program ever used the flaw is not something a version can tell. A version is read without running deno; a canary build's number is its upstream number.
